sections.label: Our Teams

briefs.headline: Alonso waits on Caicedo before Chelsea's Sunday trip to Arsenal
briefs.summary: A final call on Moises Caicedo, who lasted 13 minutes off the bench against Brighton, comes after Saturday's last training session, Xabi Alonso said Friday; Emmanuel Emegha remains out. Kickoff at the Emirates is 11:30 a.m. ET, with both clubs on six points.

briefs.headline: Isak scores twice in 10 minutes as Liverpool wins 2-0 at Ipswich
briefs.summary: Cody Gakpo set up both goals at Portman Road on Friday, Bradley Barcola made his debut off the bench in the 64th minute and Ronald Araujo made his first start; it was Andoni Iraola's first win as head coach, and Liverpool is fifth on five points.

briefs.headline: Spurs go to Forest without Maddison but with Savio back
briefs.summary: James Maddison has returned to training but is not ready for today's 10 a.m. ET kickoff at Nottingham Forest, Roberto De Zerbi said Friday; Savio is fit again and Kulusevski, Odobert and Simons remain out. Tottenham is last with no points from two matches.

briefs.headline: Brewers score five in the fifth to beat the Reds 10-7
briefs.summary: Cooper Pratt's bases-loaded triple keyed the rally Friday at Great American Ball Park after Cincinnati had led by two through three innings; Eugenio Suarez hit a three-run homer and Matt McLain also went deep for the Reds. Milwaukee (88-54) took the series opener; game two is 6:40 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Jared Jones strikes out nine as the Pirates blank the Angels 1-0
briefs.summary: Jake Mangum's second-inning double scored Konnor Griffin from first for the only run Friday at PNC Park; Jones allowed three hits in six innings and Mason Montgomery's ninth save closed Pittsburgh's ninth shutout of the season. Paul Skenes goes Sunday.

briefs.headline: Ohio opens at Nebraska with one returning offensive starter
briefs.summary: Dom Dorwart is the lone holdover on an offense led by transfer quarterback Nick Poulos for the noon ET kickoff on FS1 in Lincoln; the keys are containing Anthony Colandrea outside the pocket and running behind a new line. John Hauser said "it's not a monumental challenge."

briefs.headline: Marshall opens at Penn State in Matt Campbell's first game
briefs.summary: The Herd is a 23.5-point underdog for the 3:30 p.m. ET kickoff on FS1 at Beaver Stadium, where Tony Gibson last visited as a Michigan assistant in 2010 and called it "not a very good experience"; Penn State has 62 new players under its new coach.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati hosts D.C. United after a draw and a loss
briefs.summary: The Orange and Blue have seven wins, two losses and two draws at TQL Stadium this season and kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on Apple TV; D.C. has a league-high 10 draws under Rene Weiler. Pat Noonan said one bad performance does not force wholesale change.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Hoshoryu skips practice for the hospital; his Aki call comes Sept. 11
briefs.summary: The west yokozuna (grand champion) left Tatsunami stable for a hospital visit Saturday morning instead of training, and stablemaster Tatsunami said his entry will be decided at the Sept. 11 bout-drawing meeting: "I cannot permit entry unless he is in perfect condition." The basho (tournament) opens Sept. 13 in Tokyo, eight days out.

briefs.headline: Hakkaku says Atamifuji is 'about to go up' to ozeki
briefs.summary: The 24-year-old sekiwake (junior champion) won seven of 16 practice bouts at Friday's council session and forced out ozeki (champion) Kotozakura, and Japan Sumo Association chairman Hakkaku said "he has horsepower"; he needs 12 wins at Aki to reach the customary 33 over three tournaments.

briefs.headline: Rocchio walks off the Tigers twice as Cleveland holds the last AL wild card
briefs.summary: Brayan Rocchio hit a grand slam and a walk-off homer in a 7-6 win Friday, then scored on Travis Bazzana's 10th-inning single for a 4-3 nightcap win; the Guardians lead Toronto by a game for the third spot. Luis Campusano's 10th-inning homer beat the Yankees 3-2 in San Diego, and the Cubs (80-62) beat Miami 6-1.

briefs.headline: Hall of Fame halves its voters after the Belichick snub
briefs.summary: The Pro Football Hall of Fame cut its selection committee from 50 voters to 25, replaced the one-per-club model with at-large voters and eliminated the seniors category, effective for the Class of 2027, after Bill Belichick fell short of 80% in February; the finalist pool drops from 20 to 15.

briefs.headline: Mensah throws five touchdowns as No. 7 Miami routs Stanford 45-6
briefs.summary: Darian Mensah threw five touchdown passes in his Miami debut Friday night and Malachi Toney set a school record with 234 receiving yards as the Hurricanes won at Stanford Stadium; No. 10 Oklahoma and No. 14 USC also opened with shutouts, of UTEP and Fresno State.

sections.note: Kyodo's Hoshoryu report was read on the Kumamoto Nichinichi Shimbun, which carries its copy without a paywall; Sports Hochi and Sponichi were read on Yahoo Japan. r/Sumo was unreachable for a 13th morning.

coming_in.item: The general squirrel season opens a week from today, Sept. 12, and runs to Feb. 28: daily bag 6, possession 24, no season limit in the summary table.

coming_in.item: The youth bear weekend opens a week out, Sept. 12-13; electronic registration is required and the limits are on pamphlet page 34, not in the summary table. The second gun window, Sept. 19-25, is again in selected counties only.

prime.item: The youth weekend is today and tomorrow, Sept. 5-6: daily bag 6, possession and season limit 12, details on pamphlet page 40.

prime.item: The piers' hit-or-miss fish of the month; the Marine Fisheries limits page effective Sept. 2 lists a 12-inch fork-length minimum and 15 per day. King mackerel on the same page are 24 inches fork length, three per day, and the shops say the fall king bite has not started.

going_out.item: Day five of the two-week window, which closes at 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14: one fish per day, 15-inch minimum, harvest reporting mandatory. Marine Fisheries' annual plan review, out Friday, says the stock is showing early signs of recovery with more larger fish in the catch.
The first gun window, in SELECTED COUNTIES only, closes Monday, Sept. 7; the county list is on pamphlet pages 33-39 and not in the summary table, so none is named here. Registration is required.
going_out.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

sections.note: Bird seasons, from the agencies' own sheets: North Carolina's mourning dove, rail and gallinule seasons open today, Sept. 5, under the Wildlife Resources Commission's migratory bird proclamation (dove 15 a day, no Sunday hunting), with September teal Sept. 10-19 east of U.S. 17 and archery deer Sept. 12 in every zone. West Virginia's dove segments are Sept. 1 to Oct. 11, Nov. 2-15 and Dec. 7 to Jan. 10, 15 a day with a HIP card required, per the DNR release carried by the West Virginia Daily News on July 14. The DNR also certified a 72.75-pound blue catfish from the Ohio River in Jackson County as the state weight record, per the release carried by Lootpress on Friday. Gauley season releases from Summersville Dam begin Sept. 11, with Gauley Fest Sept. 17-20 in Summersville, per West Virginia Explorer.

waters.working: Down from 65.6 cfs a day ago and the lowest reading of the week - the river is a string of pools now, and every trout in it is looking up. Long leader to 6X, a single ant or beetle dropped tight to the undercut banks, and a small olive sculpin swung slow through the plunge pools that still hold depth. Caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage here; at this flow the terrestrials falling off the bank are what the fish see most.
waters.note: The Forest Service's phased closure of Forest Road 86, the Williams River Road, from FR 216 to Route 150 was posted to end Aug. 31 and is still listed; the agency says recreation sites stay reachable from Dyer on the west. The Tea Creek Campground bridge replacement continues with the campground open through the work zone.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 25.3 ft and rising - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up from 24.83 feet a day ago, so a touch more push on the pool than yesterday - the wing-dam tips and the riprap are the structure and shad the forage, so a white swimbait or a spoon over the tips at first light, then a football jig dragged down the seam once the sun is on the water.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 27.0 ft and rising - normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up from 25.81 feet a day ago, more than a foot below the dam, so there is real current on the lock wall and in the barge cuts again - a crawfish-colored jig pitched into the slack behind the cuts and a skipjack-pattern swimbait along the riprap where the flow pins bait against it.

waters.reading: Sound highs 3:08 AM at 3.3 ft and 3:50 PM at 4.5 ft at Hampstead; lows 9:36 AM at 0.3 ft and 10:47 PM at 0.8 ft.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 3:08 AM and 3:50 PM in the sound.
waters.working: The Fisherman's Post September report, published Tuesday and four days old, has red drum "steady when fishing docks and creek mouths" on early topwater, flounder "all over the place" with an excellent class of 20-to-24-inch fish on a bucktail and Gulp trailer, black drum and pompano on the bottom off the Surf City pier, and Spanish and blues hit-or-miss on plugs off the Jolly Roger; the shops are still waiting on the fall king bite. Coastal Angler's September note adds black drum on cut shrimp at the bridges and oyster rocks. Flounder want moving water on structure, so work the flood into the 3:50 PM high; reds want the last of the fall, into tonight's 10:47 PM low. Waning crescent at 40%, so neap tides and a gentle inlet. Water 85.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and the read that matters; the oceanfront pier runs well ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. NWS Wilmington's 5 a.m. surf zone forecast has a moderate rip current risk on Pender beaches with 1-to-2-foot surf, and a Heat Advisory covers coastal Pender from 11 a.m. to 8 p.m. with heat index values to 110; Newport's advisory for coastal Onslow runs to 6 p.m. Marine Fisheries reopened a portion of Topsail Sound, Virginia and Beckys creeks, Stump Sound and Alligator Bay to shellfishing at sunrise today under proclamation PA-45-2026; the ICW stretch from Green Channel to the Figure Eight bridge stays closed.

kicker: Hoshoryu's Aki entry is decided at the Sept. 11 bout-drawing meeting, two days before the tournament opens.
